answer: Proof-of-service bandwidth checks resist sybils: each identity must continuously relay a verifiable share of network traffic, audited by peers like light through a prism that reveals whether a beam is real or copied, so one machine cannot pretend to be thousands of agents. An attacker wanting ten thousand personas must supply ten thousand shares of bandwidth across the lagoon of relays, turning free keys into metered pipes, while one honest agent serves once. The limit is access: low-bandwidth agents need a yarrow-lined light tier, or the gate favours data centres over honest small operators.
